# T008 — Repair frontend delivery-tool advisory chain

## Summary

Fixed the root critical `shell-quote` chain without updating or downgrading the SWA CLI: npm refreshed the transitive package inside `concurrently`'s existing compatible range. Root audit changed from **3 critical / 26 high / 7 moderate / 3 low (39 affected package entries)** to **2 critical / 26 high / 7 moderate / 3 low (38 entries)**. Standalone backend remains **0 / 6 / 0 / 0**. Counts are affected package entries, not independent advisories; neither lock is clean.

## Changes

- `package-lock.json`: `npm update shell-quote --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` changed only `shell-quote` 1.8.3 → 1.12.0 among resolved packages. npm 11 also removed a redundant root `dependencies` record for the pinned Rollup Linux binary; the root manifest's `optionalDependencies` and its lock record remain unchanged. No manifest, backend lock, SWA settings, runtime code, tests or deployment scripts changed.
- `.github/modernization/28793a23-310c-4415-b15a-e1692e8530cc/progress/T008.md`: remediation and both-lock scan evidence.

## Decisions

On **2026-10-20**, Node **24.21.0** / npm **11.19.0**, `npm explain shell-quote` traced `frontend (dev) → @azure/static-web-apps-cli@2.0.7 → concurrently@7.6.0 → shell-quote@1.8.3`. The latest published SWA CLI 2.1.0 still declares `concurrently: ^7.6.0`, whose `shell-quote: ^1.7.3` already admits the patched 1.x release. An in-range lock refresh is smaller than changing the direct CLI, introducing an override, or migrating concurrently's major. npm resolved 1.12.0, a current compatible 1.x release rather than the first jointly patched 1.9.0. No `--force`, audit ignore or nodemon downgrade. [Node's release schedule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/Release/main/schedule.json) lists the already-pinned Node 24 LTS through 2028-04-30; this task did not change runtime pins.

Live [GitHub Advisory Database](https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p) and [second advisory](https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv) API records confirm the ranges and patches below (npm's initial root audit agreed). The critical injection requires an attacker-controlled *object token* `.op` passed through `quote()` into a shell; the high-severity DoS requires attacker-influenced strings passed to `parse()`. This path is a **local frontend delivery/dev CLI dependency**, not a frontend production HTTP handler, and no external inputs to these methods were established in the app; reachability in developer/deployment environments is not ruled out. No advisory is dismissed merely for being dev-only.

| Advisory | Severity | Package | From → to | Direct / transitive; first patched | Status / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p) / CVE-2026-9277 | Critical | shell-quote | 1.8.3 → 1.12.0 | SWA CLI → concurrently; 1.8.4 | **Fixed**: absent from root rescan; verified object-token `quote()` injection range `>=1.1.0 <=1.8.3`. |
| [GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv) / CVE-2026-13311 | High | shell-quote | 1.8.3 → 1.12.0 | Same chain; 1.9.0 (first version fixing **both**) | **Fixed**: absent from root rescan; quadratic `parse()` range `<=1.8.4`. |

## Follow-ups and risks

- **Open, owner decision required, not accepted/suppressed:** root critical `tinypool` ([GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3), [GHSA-85c8-ppgw-ccpr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-85c8-ppgw-ccpr)) and derived critical `vitest` entry (also including [GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9), `@vitest/mocker` moderate). Test-runner prototype pollution needs a primitive in the test process; the mocker needs a reachable dev socket; offline tests establish neither exposure nor safety. A separate characterized Vitest major upgrade is needed; do not force audit's major suggestion.
- **Open SWA delivery-tool family:** `@azure/static-web-apps-cli@2.0.7` high derived entry still includes `adm-zip@0.5.16` high (eight advisories, e.g. [GHSA-8238-w5pm-2374](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8238-w5pm-2374), malicious ZIP extraction input), `devcert@1.2.2` low → `tmp@0.0.33` high ([GHSA-52f5-9888-hmc6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-52f5-9888-hmc6), [GHSA-ph9p-34f9-6g65](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ph9p-34f9-6g65), local temporary-file abuse), and `cookie@0.5.0` low ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x), untrusted cookie values). These are dev CLI dependencies, potentially reachable during local/deployment tooling use, **not proven unreachable**. CLI 2.1.0 does not remove the concurrently path; `adm-zip` needs >=0.6.1 beyond CLI's `^0.5.14`, and `cookie` >=0.7.0 beyond CLI's `^0.5.0`. Do not blindly override these behavior-sensitive ranges: characterize ZIP/config/deployment flows and seek upstream-compatible versions or a planned targeted override with tests. Root Express has separately patched cookie 0.7.2.
- **Other open root affected entries:** high `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin`, `@typescript-eslint/parser`, `@typescript-eslint/type-utils`, `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree`, `@typescript-eslint/utils`, `axios`, `brace-expansion`, `braces`, `browserslist`, `chokidar`, `fast-glob`, `flatted`, `form-data`, `glob`, `joi`, `js-yaml`, `lodash`, `micromatch`, `minimatch`, `node-forge`, `nodemon`, `picomatch`, `typescript-eslint`; moderate `@humanfs/node`, `ajv`, `baseline-browser-mapping`, `fast-copy`, `follow-redirects`, `yaml`; low `@babel/core`. Standalone backend remains high `brace-expansion`, `braces`, `chokidar`, `minimatch`, `nodemon`, `picomatch`. All per-package IDs, installed nodes, ranges and fix metadata remain in raw both-lock scan JSON. Lint/build/test dependencies require separate scoped remediation and characterization; input-controlled globs, archive/network parsing, and externally accessible developer tools are potential paths, not proven production exposures.
- npm's backend `nodemon@1.14.10` major **downgrade** suggestion for chokidar/braces is not a safe automatic fix; no backend manifest/lock was modified. Follow up with owner on targeted in-range fixes, tested overrides or upstream parent releases. None of these findings has an owner-approved acceptance, ignored audit result, or established live Azure/deployment reachability.
